title: Importing Samples & Trade Fair Goods Through Turkish Customs (ATA Carnet)
seoTitle: ATA Carnet Turkey Customs: Trade Fair & Sample Guide
metaDescription: Learn when exhibitors need an ATA Carnet for Turkey customs, rules for luggage samples, IST cargo tips, and hiring a licensed customs broker.
quickAnswer: Foreign exhibitors bringing demonstration machines, prototypes, or commercial samples to Türkiye temporarily should obtain an ATA Carnet from their home chamber of commerce before departure. Recognized by [TOBB](https://tobb.org.tr/TIRIslemleriMudurlugu/ATA/Sayfalar/Eng/AnaSayfa.php) under the Istanbul Convention, the carnet lets qualifying goods enter duty-free for up to one year provided every serial-numbered item is re-exported intact.

body.text: Bringing demonstration hardware or commercial samples to an Istanbul exhibition requires advance customs planning. At [Itinerary of Türkiye](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/), our two founders coordinate business travel logistics and on-the-ground introductions on a transparent, client-paid flat fee ("Paid by our clients. Independent of provider commissions."). We do not act as customs brokers or legal counsel; all tariff classifications, temporary import declarations, and compliance decisions belong strictly to licensed Turkish customs brokers (gümrük müşaviri), attorneys, and the [Republic of Türkiye Ministry of Trade](https://ticaret.gov.tr/gumruk-islemleri).
When do trade-fair exhibitors need an ATA Carnet for demo equipment?

Exhibitors need an ATA Carnet whenever they temporarily bring reusable commercial goods—such as machinery, medical devices, audiovisual gear, or high-value product prototypes—into Türkiye for trade shows, technical demonstrations, or buyer meetings without paying local import duties and VAT deposits. The carnet acts as a unified customs passport backed by an international guarantee chain.

In Türkiye, the national guaranteeing association is the [Union of Chambers and Commodity Exchanges of Türkiye (TOBB)](https://tobb.org.tr/TIRIslemleriMudurlugu/ATA/Sayfalar/ATANedir.php). Türkiye accepts ATA Carnets for three core categories: commercial samples, exhibitions and fairs, and professional equipment. Consumables, printed brochures handed out to visitors, food tastings, and items intended for sale cannot travel on a carnet; those require permanent import clearance and applicable duties.

body.text: What customs rules apply to carrying commercial samples in luggage?

Passenger duty-free allowances under [Ministry of Trade passenger exemptions](https://ticaret.gov.tr/gumruk-islemleri/sikca-sorulan-sorular/bireysel/yolcu-muafiyetleri) cover only non-commercial personal items in modest quantities. Commercial samples carried in checked suitcases or carry-on bags fall outside personal allowances and must be declared at the airport Red Channel upon arrival, either under an ATA Carnet or through a formal temporary import procedure.

According to the [Ministry of Trade Customs Guide](https://gumrukrehberi.gov.tr/sayfa/yolcu-e%C5%9Fyas%C4%B1-nedir), goods showing commercial volume or commercial purpose are treated as trade cargo rather than passenger belongings. If an exhibitor arrives with an ATA Carnet in hand luggage, customs officers verify the physical items against the General List, stamp the white importation voucher, and record the re-export deadline. Skipping the departure exit stamp when flying home leaves the carnet open in Turkish customs records and can trigger a claim against your home chamber guarantee.
How do you avoid shipment delays at IST cargo customs?

Preventing clearance holds at Istanbul Airport (IST) cargo terminals starts two to three weeks before your flight. Match every serial number, HS code, weight, and declared value across the ATA Carnet General List, airway bill, and packing list, and appoint a Turkish customs broker with power of attorney before freight departs your origin hub.
Pre-Shipment Checklist for IST Cargo Clearance:

items: Verify that the named holder or authorized representative on Box B of the ATA Carnet matches the licensed broker or traveler presenting the goods.
Confirm that every electronic or mechanical unit displays a legible serial plate matching the General List line by line.
Separate giveaways, stand graphics, and consumables onto a separate commercial invoice rather than mixing them into carnet crates.
Check whether specialized items (such as radio-frequency gear, batteries, or medical demos) require Ministry of Trade TAREKS or ministerial pre-approvals.
Schedule freight arrival at least five business days before booth build-up to absorb warehouse handling and physical inspection queues.

body.text: Which licensed customs brokers (gümrük müşaviri) should be engaged?

Foreign companies should engage an independent, Ministry-licensed customs broker (gümrük müşaviri) registered with a regional chamber such as the [Istanbul Customs Brokers Association (İGMD)](https://www.igmd.org.tr/). Verify the firm's active membership on the [İGMD directory](https://www.igmd.org.tr/firma-bul?p=10), confirm direct experience with ATA Carnet temporary imports at IST, and request an itemized written fee schedule before issuing authorization.

Official exhibition freight forwarders assigned by a fair organizer can be convenient for on-site forklift drayage inside the hall, but exhibitors are free to compare independent customs brokers for airport clearance. faq.q: How long is an ATA Carnet valid in Türkiye?
faq.a: An ATA Carnet is valid for up to 12 months from its issue date, though Turkish customs officers at the port of entry may set a shorter re-export window aligned with your trade-fair dates. Always check the exact final re-export date stamped on the importation counterfoil.

faq.q: Can I sell a sample imported under an ATA Carnet during a Turkish trade fair?
faq.a: No, carnet goods are admitted strictly for temporary use and must be re-exported. Converting a carnet item into a local sale requires prior customs approval, formal permanent import clearance through a licensed customs broker, and payment of all duties and taxes.

faq.q: Do I need a Turkish power of attorney for a customs broker at IST?
faq.a: Yes. If cargo arrives as air freight rather than accompanied luggage, your Turkish customs broker needs a formal authorization (and typically a notarized or apostilled power of attorney, depending on the procedure) to represent the carnet holder before customs.

faq.q: What happens if I forget to get my ATA Carnet stamped when leaving Türkiye?
faq.a: Without a Turkish customs re-exportation stamp, the carnet remains open and TOBB may issue a regularisation claim for unpaid duties and penalties. You would then need to submit secondary proof of re-importation from your home customs authority to resolve the claim.

faq.q: Are printed catalogues and promotional giveaways covered by an ATA Carnet?
faq.a: No. Consumable or disposable items—including brochures, branded gifts, and food or beverage samples—are excluded from the ATA Carnet system and must be declared separately under standard import rules.

faq.q: Does Itinerary of Türkiye handle customs declarations directly?
faq.a: No. Itinerary of Türkiye coordinates business travel schedules, exhibition ground logistics, and introductions to independent licensed professionals. Formal customs declarations, tariff rulings, and legal filings are handled exclusively by licensed Turkish customs brokers (gümrük müşaviri) and attorneys.
